plan.title: Zebrafish larvae drug-exposure DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single bulk RNA-seq experiment: gene-level raw integer counts from Salmon on the Ensembl Danio rerio annotation (counts.csv, 12,000 genes x 6 samples, first column gene symbol) with a 6-row metadata table carrying one condition column — 3 drug-exposed vs 3 control whole-larvae pools, unpaired, one batch. The research question is two-part (which genes differ, which pathways they point to), so the plan is a straight DESeq2 two-group contrast followed by preranked enrichment, plus a report.

T1S1 runs sample-structure QC before any test: library sizes, blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, and a sample-to-sample distance heatmap, coloured by condition. With n=3 per group this is the only chance to see an outlier pool or a swapped label before it silently drives the contrast; there is no batch column to check, so condition is the only annotation available.

T1S2 does the modelling. Counts are already gene-level summaries of Salmon output, so no tximport step is possible here — the transcript-level quantifications and average transcript lengths are not among the inputs, which means the length offset recommended for Salmon input cannot be applied; the step must state that limitation rather than fabricate offsets. Pre-filter is minimal (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, the smallest group size), normalization is DESeq2's median-of-ratios size factors inside the model (counts are not pre-scaled), design is ~condition with the control level set explicitly as the reference so that a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated. Wald test, apeglm shrinkage of the treated-vs-control coefficient, BH adjustment with independent filtering at alpha 0.05, p-value histogram inspected before adjustment. edgeR quasi-likelihood is run on the same filtered matrix as a second method and the intersection is reported as the high-confidence set. Three replicates per group is low power: the benchmark literature says a test of this size recovers only a minority of true DE genes, mostly large-fold-change ones, so absence from the list is not evidence of no change, and the threshold must not be loosened to compensate.

T2S1 handles pathways. This is the weak point of a zebrafish analysis and the plan is explicit about it: no curated Danio rerio gene set collection is present in the reference store (I checked — pathways cover human, mouse and rat only; there is no zebrafish GMT and no zebrafish-to-human ortholog table). Two routes remain, and the step runs both and reports them side by side. Route A maps zebrafish symbols to human orthologs (org.Dr.eg.db plus babelgene, both installed) and runs fgsea against the staged human collections — MSigDB Hallmark 2026.1, GO-BP 2026.1, WikiPathways 2026.07.10. Route B stays native and runs a GO enrichment on the Danio rerio annotation in org.Dr.eg.db. Each has a stated limit: the ortholog route drops every gene without a one-to-one human ortholog (zebrafish has widespread duplicate paralogs from the teleost genome duplication, so the loss is substantial and must be counted), and the native zebrafish GO annotation is thinner than the human one. The ranked list is the full set of tested genes ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic — a stated choice among the three defensible metrics, taken because it scales effect by its uncertainty and does not saturate into ties. Size window 15-500 after intersection with the tested genes, redundant significant sets collapsed. An over-representation test on the significant gene list only runs if that list exceeds ~50 genes; at n=3 it may well not, and the step must say so rather than report an empty hypergeometric result as a finding.

T1S3 assembles the report: fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot), the gene table carrying unshrunken log2FC, shrunken log2FC and lfcSE with genes ranked on the shrunken value, DESeq2/edgeR overlap counts, the count of NA p-values split by cause (Cook's outlier flag versus independent filtering), leading-edge genes per significant set, the annotation and identifier-space statement required for a non-model-collection organism, the power statement, and a full reproducibility record with seeds and package and collection versions.

Markdown report with fit diagnostics, gene tables with shrunken and unshrunken LFC, leading-edge genes, power statement, reproducibility record

Take the full ranked list of tested genes from T1S2 (every gene that survived filtering, ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic) and run enrichment by two independent routes, reporting both.

Route A (ortholog): map Danio rerio gene symbols to human orthologs, keeping one-to-one orthologs only, then run fgsea preranked against human curated collections — a hallmark collection, a GO biological-process collection, and a community-curated pathway collection, all resolved from the reference store at run time. Count and report how many zebrafish genes entered, how many mapped, and how many were dropped for lacking a one-to-one human ortholog.

Route B (native): run GO enrichment on the same ranked list using the Danio rerio organism annotation package directly, with no ortholog step.

Apply a gene set size window of 15-500 AFTER intersecting each set with the tested genes, BH-adjust, and collapse significant sets that share most of their leading-edge genes into groups with one representative each. Emit, per significant set: name, size, NES, p, padj, and the leading-edge genes with their Wald statistics. Report the overlap and the disagreement between the two routes.
steps.context: Danio rerio is not human or mouse, and no curated zebrafish gene set collection is staged in the reference store — the pathway collections present cover human (MSigDB hallmark, GO BP/CC/MF, WikiPathways, KEGG MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID), mouse and rat only, and no zebrafish-to-human ortholog table is staged either. The ortholog map must therefore come from the installed annotation packages (org.Dr.eg.db for zebrafish identifiers, babelgene for ortholog mapping), and the native route uses the GO annotation inside org.Dr.eg.db. Both routes are compromised in different ways, which is why both run.
acceptance_criteria: Ranked list is the FULL set of tested genes from T1S2 ranked by the Wald statistic — not a thresholded list
Ortholog mapping reports: n zebrafish genes in, n mapped one-to-one, n dropped, and the percentage retained
Route A fgsea run against at least a hallmark collection and a GO biological-process collection resolved from the reference store, with the collection name and version recorded for each
Route B GO enrichment run on the native Danio rerio annotation, with the annotation package version recorded
Size window 15-500 applied after intersection with the tested genes; BH adjustment applied within each collection
Significant sets (padj < 0.05) reported with NES and leading-edge gene lists; redundant sets collapsed with one representative per group and the full table kept as a supplement
Overlap between Route A and Route B results reported, and disagreement stated rather than hidden
If fewer than 50 genes reached padj < 0.05 in T1S2, no over-representation test is run on that list and the report says so explicitly
If a named reference collection cannot be resolved at run time, the step reports which one was missing and continues with those that resolved
constraints: Rank metric is the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the stat column) — this is a stated choice among three defensible metrics, taken because it scales the effect by its uncertainty and does not saturate into ties the way a signed p-value does. Do not rank by the unshrunken log2 fold change alone
Do not truncate the ranked list by padj or fold change before fgsea
For any over-representation test, the universe is the genes tested in T1S2 — never the whole genome or the whole annotation

Resolve every gene set collection from the reference store by what it is (hallmark sets, GO biological process sets, community-curated pathway sets) for the species of the mapped identifiers; never hard-code a path
Human collections use HGNC symbols in upper case — match case after ortholog mapping or the intersection silently returns empty
Set and record a random seed; fgsea permutation p-values are not reproducible without it
Record the collection name and version for every collection used
caveats: The ortholog route drops every zebrafish gene without a one-to-one human ortholog. The teleost whole-genome duplication left many zebrafish genes as paralog pairs, so the loss is substantial and non-random — the surviving set is biased toward genes with simple orthology, which is a real limit on interpretation
The native zebrafish GO annotation is thinner than the human one; a real process can go undetected simply because few zebrafish genes carry the term
Enrichment results are method-dependent — a ranked test and an over-representation test on the same data give different lists. Present each set as a hypothesis for follow-up, not as a proven finding
GO is a nested hierarchy: parent and child sets share members, so a block of significant related terms is one finding, not many
Count-based gene lists are biased toward long and highly expressed genes; the ranked test on the tested-gene universe mitigates but does not remove this

grounding.reason: Preranked fgsea on the full tested list per R-0107@976c and R-0045@f652; for a non-human non-mouse organism R-0050@0763 requires either a human ortholog map or the organism's GO annotation, and both routes run with their limits stated. Disputed rank metric R-0108@409f resolved in favour of the DESeq2 Wald statistic, consistent with R-0099@0a77.

steps.name: Consolidated report
steps.question: What is the reproducible, honestly-caveated account of the treated-vs-control zebrafish larvae contrast and its pathway interpretation?
steps.description: Assemble a single markdown report from the T1S1, T1S2 and T2S1 outputs. Order: (1) design, method and package versions, thresholds, number of genes tested after filtering, number of DE genes per direction; (2) the power statement for 3 replicates per group, placed BEFORE the gene tables; (3) QC figures and the outlier verdict; (4) fit diagnostics — MA plot and dispersion plot, each with a sentence on what it shows; (5) p-value histogram and its shape; (6) gene table ranked on the shrunken log2 fold change, carrying unshrunken log2FC, shrunken log2FC and lfcSE side by side, with the shrinkage estimator named in the header; (7) DESeq2/edgeR overlap with the intersection named as the high-confidence set; (8) NA p-value counts split by cause; (9) enrichment results from both routes with database name and version, rank metric, universe and size window stated, and leading-edge genes per significant set with overlaps between sets marked; (10) annotation statement — annotation source, release, identifier space, the ortholog map used and the share of genes that mapped; (11) reproducibility record — sessionInfo, seeds, package versions, collection versions.
steps.context: Zebrafish (Danio rerio) whole-larvae drug-exposure study, 3 treated vs 3 control pools, 12,000 genes. Two things must not be softened in this report: the low power of an n=3 design, and the fact that pathway interpretation rests on either a lossy zebrafish-to-human ortholog map or a thin native GO annotation, because no curated zebrafish gene set collection exists in this environment.
acceptance_criteria: Report names the method, every package version, the design formula, the contrast direction (treated vs control), the thresholds, the number of genes tested and the number of DE genes per direction
Power statement for 3 replicates per group appears before the gene tables and says plainly that absence from the DE list is not evidence of no change
MA plot and dispersion plot both present with a one-line reading of each
Gene table carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE, is ranked on the shrunken value, and names apeglm as the estimator
Enrichment section states database, version, rank metric, universe and size window, lists leading-edge genes per significant set, and marks leading-edge overlap between reported sets
Enrichment section states the method-dependence caveat and reports the Route A / Route B overlap and disagreement
Annotation section states source, release, identifier space, the ortholog map and the mapped share
Reproducibility record with sessionInfo, seeds, package versions and collection versions stored alongside the results
constraints: Rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken log2 fold change; keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit
Do not present the DESeq2/edgeR union as the result — the intersection is the high-confidence set
State the size of the significant gene list before any pathway claim
Do not describe an enriched set as a mechanism; present it as a hypothesis for follow-up
If any step upstream reported a missing reference collection or an unmapped gene fraction, carry that forward verbatim rather than summarising it away
caveats: Whole-larvae pooling means tissue-specific effects are diluted; a pathway hit cannot be localised to an organ from this data
No dose, timepoint or compound identity is present in the metadata, so the report cannot state exposure conditions beyond treated versus control

grounding.reason: Report content follows the returned report-step rules: power statement at n=3 (R-0094@6849), two-method overlap (R-0042@54e1), shrunken and unshrunken effect columns (R-0085@c24d), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087@c53d), enrichment provenance and leading edge (R-0051@01ca, R-0105@c4a8), non-human annotation statement (R-0081@5c95), reproducibility record (R-0086@becf).
